q: I think the reality of being pregnant was quite a wake up call. Such a wanted baby, but wow, it's different actually living it.
cx: Five days after her first birth in the UK, looking back on the pregnancy.

q: This was not my birth plan. Infact the literal opposite of what I wanted. I was devastated and terrified about it. Little did I know, even if I read about others experiences, it really was so calm and settled.
cx: How a booked surgical birth she dreaded actually felt.

q: Labour recovery ward was a saga I'd dread if I got pregnant again, I now understand the horror stories
cx: The one part of her NHS birth she would dread repeating.

q: I was in a room with 3 other women, partners with them. It was boiling hot and no air circulation.
cx: Describing the NHS postnatal ward to a pregnant reader.

q: Best advice, bring a small fan or two, bring a pillow, bring one or two comfortable outfits and bring a variety of snack options.
cx: What she would pack for a UK postnatal ward.

q: I was so scared the whole time... like I couldnt stop thinking about how awful pushing was going to be.
cx: First birth, written hours afterwards; she had hoped to avoid an epidural.

q: Every other contraction and push I groaned through like i practiced.
cx: Practised breathing and sounds carried her through labour.

q: I always thought I was the biggest wuss ever and apparently I championed through dispite doubting myself the entire time.
cx: How she saw herself before and after her first labour.

q: The only way this happened is because I put all my focus into each contraction, taking one at a time, I listened to my body when I felt the need to move, and most importantly, the nursing staff was PHENOMENALLY supportive and helpful.
cx: What she credits for getting through.

q: My husband (who works in the medical field and has attended quite a few births) couldnt stop saying how impressed he was with me
cx: What her husband said after the birth.

q: As someone with a lifelong fear, and bad history, with doctors and hospitals i felt so safe and supported throughout my labor.
cx: Feeling safe in hospital despite a long fear of them.

q: I was so scared because you hear so much bad regarding birth stories, and dont get me wrong it was definitely intense and hard at times, but once it was over it was like, woah, I did that!
cx: Why she shared her positive story.

q: I went in with the goal of having a natural birth, but unfortunately, I progressed extremely quickly and my contractions were coming one after another with virtually no breaks in between.
cx: First birth; her plan changed when labour came fast.

q: Once it kicked in, I was in absolute BLISS. 😂 It was such a relief after having contractions back to back with no real breaks.
cx: How the epidural felt after hours of fast contractions.

q: Despite that, I can honestly say that my birth experience was NOT traumatic. It was intense, painful, and definitely not what I expected, but I would 100% do it all over again.
cx: Her verdict on her first birth despite a serious tear.

q: My husband has been a life saver. He cooks and cleans, makes up little songs about her, takes her away so I’m forced to recharge and nap even if I just wanna spend all my time with her.
cx: Six days after an unplanned surgical birth, what her husband does at home.

q: I’m so tired i don’t know what to do with myself but I’ve never been happier.
cx: Her first week with the baby.

q: I’ve been pretty vocal in this thread while pregnant and I remember being **desperate** for any positive stories about having a baby, cause all I’ve read was literal horrors lol.
cx: Five months postpartum, recalling what she searched for while pregnant.

q: He didn’t want to take care of our son, he was constantly irritated, tired, even screaming and saying the meanest shit I’ve ever heard him say. We’ve been together for 12 years, he was literally perfect during my pregnancy, so I thought we were covered.
cx: Her husband struggled in the first weeks; it improved months later.
r: partner mental health / relationship conflict in unit

q: My core and abdominal muscles are gone. Not slightly less strong -GONE. I was not expecting that and the recovery is a pain in the ass.
cx: What surprised her about recovery.

q: Stop spending all that money on contrast cards and other toys that supposedly develop your baby’s skills. Its skills will come one way or another.
cx: Advice to pregnant readers on what not to buy.

q: I really wanted this second time to be my redemptive birth that I wanted the first time. Well it was redemptive but not exactly what I had planned.
cx: Second birth after a hard first one; labour was very fast.

q: This low pain tolerance mama freaked out into total panic mode and I was also just mad/angry too. I kept telling my husband we waited to leave too late and I couldn’t do this.
cx: Arriving too late for the pain relief she had planned.

q: While it’s not what I planned it was a great birth and honestly I would do it over again compared to my first!
cx: Comparing her second birth with her first.

q: just wanted to share to all the second time moms out there, pack your hospital bag early and prepare for a quick delivery just in case! You just never know and mentally prepare for all possibilities!
cx: Her advice to other second-time mothers.

q: They kept emphasizing this and saying my risk was so low.
cx: Doctors pushed one birth route in her second pregnancy after a frightening first birth.

q: The entire pregnancy my gut told me c section. I had a harder pregnancy and was way bigger than my first. However, I felt pressured to choose vaginal.
cx: Torn between doctors' advice and her own instinct second time round.

q: I decided to go with a section for my peace of mind and what felt like more control of the situation.
cx: Why she chose her second birth route.
r: prior birth complication; c-section decision; therapy mentioned

q: I kept being told to hold my breath and not make noise which was annoying.
cx: What staff told her while pushing during her first birth.

q: Think I only survived because of my angel of a nurse, every time I said "I can't do this" she said "don't say you can't because you are."
cx: The nurse's words she credits for getting through labour.
